title: Psychological support online with a psychologist in Italy – Blooming
description: Psychological support with a psychologist and psychotherapist, for a hard time: illness in the family, bereavement, separation, job loss, infertility, a new baby, a move. Online. Free 30-minute first meeting.

data.title: Support for a specific hard time, from an illness in the family to a move.

p.t: Psychological support is for something you're going through now: a loss, a separation, a baby, a family member who is seriously ill. It's with a psychologist and psychotherapist with clinical experience in hospitals, clinics and private practice, online by video call.

data.title: A hard time can weigh more when the people you'd lean on are far away.

items.title: Someone in your family is seriously ill

p.t: It may be a physical illness or a mental one, in a parent, a partner, a sibling or a child. If you're far away, you get news second-hand and in fragments, and every decision about whether to fly back carries guilt either way. If they're here with you, you may be doing most of the caring alone, with doctors who speak a language you're still learning.

items.title: You've lost someone, and the people around you didn't know them

p.t: Maybe you couldn't get to the funeral, or you went and came back to a life where nobody had met the person you're grieving. Grief doesn't follow the timetable of a working week, and it can be lonelier when the people who'd share it are in another country.

items.title: A relationship or a job has ended, and so has the reason you came

p.t: If you moved for a partner or a job, losing either one can raise a bigger question: whether to stay at all. You're dealing with the loss and with a decision about your whole life at the same time.

items.title: Trying for a baby is taking longer than you hoped

p.t: Tests and treatment bring months of waiting, often with appointments and results in Italian. Each month can bring hope and then disappointment, and it isn't always easy to talk about with the people around you.

items.title: A baby is on the way, or has just arrived, and your own family is far away

p.t: Sleepless nights come without anyone to drop round with food or take a turn. The mix of happiness and worry can be hard to share when the people you'd usually share it with are a flight away.

items.title: The move itself is heavier than you expected

p.t: It was your choice, and by most measures it's going well. Still, you feel off balance, you miss people more than you thought you would, and small things that used to be easy now take effort.
None of these stays neatly in one part of your life. A bereavement shows up at your desk, and losing a job changes how things are at home, so the sessions can cover both.

data.title: Psychological support focuses on what's happening now.

p.t: Psychological support focuses on getting through a specific hard time. It looks at the situation you're in now and how you're coping with it, rather than at difficulties that go back a long way.

items.title: The first sessions: what's happening and what you need

p.t: Your psychologist asks about what's going on and how it's affecting you day to day, including who you can count on, here and at home. Together you agree what you'd like the sessions to help with.

items.title: Then sessions shaped around your situation

p.t: Some sessions are space to say what you can't say elsewhere. Others are more practical: how to manage sleep and worry; how to make a decision you keep putting off, such as whether to travel home; how to talk to the people around you, an employer included, about what you're going through.

items.note: Specific techniques: to confirm with Monica.

items.title: A check on how it's going

p.t: Along the way, you and your psychologist look at whether the sessions are helping and what you still need. If something longer would help more, she will tell you (see below).

data.title: A psychologist who is also a psychotherapist.

people.name: Psychological support and psychotherapy

p.t: Psychological support is with a psychologist, registered with the Italian Order of Psychologists since 2010, who is a cognitive behavioural psychotherapist. Her clinical experience includes hospital psychology, clinics and private practice. She works with a bio-psycho-social approach, explained on the psychotherapy page. She also has an MSc in work and organisational psychology.
